before.title: Frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pairs and their real-field encoding
before.reference: scaffold-added necessary formulation prerequisite for the vector PEC scattering theorem (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
before.statement: Let $\omega>0$, let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set, and let $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ be the vacuum constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Phasor encoding] For every pair of $C^\infty$ maps $\widetilde E,\widetilde B:D\to\mathbb C^3$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) define the **associated real fields** $$E(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t}\bigr),\qquad B(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\widetilde B(x)e^{-i\omega t}\bigr)\qquad((x,t)\in D\times\mathbb R),$$ componentwise, with the complex exponential and real part of [[def-complex-exponential]] and [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]; this is the encoding convention of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] specialized from plane-wave amplitudes to a general $C^\infty$ amplitude, and the complex fields are not themselves physical fields. (b) [Source-free class] The pair $(\widetilde E,\widetilde B)$ is called a **frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on $D$** when it is $C^\infty$ and satisfies, on $D$, $$\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}\widetilde B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=i\omega\widetilde B,\qquad \operatorname{curl}\widetilde B=-i\omega\varepsilon_0\mu_0\widetilde E=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E,$$ with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] applied componentwise to the complex fields. The word 'source-free' records that the displayed equations carry no charge or current term; the associated real fields are read as an electric and a magnetic field of [[def-em-fields]], $\omega$ is the angular frequency and $T:=2\pi/\omega$ the period. (c) [Status and scope] This item fixes the encoding, the four phasor equations and the terminology only. It asserts no equation for the associated real fields, no outgoing or boundary condition, no existence or uniqueness statement, no energy or flux reading and no empirical content. In particular the deduction that the associated real fields satisfy the smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations with zero sources is not part of this definition; for the pairs used on this page it is established by the exterior-scattering theorem recorded later on this page. Only $C^\infty$ pairs on an open set are defined, so no boundary trace, weak or distributional class is introduced here.
before.strategy: This is a definition contract assembled from earlier items; well-definedness is discharged by the cited suppliers. (i) The encoding (a) is the real-part-of-complex-amplitude convention of [[def-em-complex-plane-wave]] with a general $C^\infty$ spatial amplitude; the componentwise real part of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and the complex exponential of [[def-complex-exponential]] are total on $\mathbb C^3$, so the associated real fields are defined for every $C^\infty$ pair, with no equation assumed. (ii) The class (b) is cut out by four equations on the open set $D$: the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] act componentwise on the $C^\infty$ complex fields, and the two constants satisfy $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=c^{-2}$ by [[def-em-si-conventions]]; the displayed third and fourth equations use only complex scalar multiplication, so the class is well-defined without any choice principle. (iii) The physical reading of the associated real fields as an electric and a magnetic field uses [[def-em-fields]]; the units of $\widetilde E$ are V$\,$m$^{-1}$ and those of $\widetilde B$ are T, inherited from that definition. (iv) Clause (c) records exactly what is not asserted; in particular the complex Maxwell-to-real-Maxwell deduction is deliberately left to a consumer, because a definition must not assert the field equations of its associated real fields.

before.title: Real parts of $e^{-i\omega t}$ phasors: calculus, injectivity and equivalence with the real Helmholtz-Maxwell system
before.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the vector PEC scattering theorem (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-40.notes.md)
before.statement: Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $c>0$ and $\omega>0$, and let $\widetilde E,\widetilde B:D\to\mathbb C^3$. Define $E,B:D\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R^3$ by $E(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and $B(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde B(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ componentwise ([[def-complex-exponential]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]; [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] for the classes). Then: (a) [Calculus] if $\widetilde E,\widetilde B$ are $C^1$, then $E,B$ are $C^1$ and at every $(x,t)\in D\times\mathbb R$: $\partial_tE(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(-i\omega\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and likewise for $B$; for each $j\in\{1,2,3\}$, $\partial_jE(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\partial_j\widetilde E(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and likewise for $B$; and with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] acting on the spatial variable, $\operatorname{div}E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{div}\widetilde E)(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, $\operatorname{curl}E(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E)(x)e^{-i\omega t})$, and likewise for $B$. (b) [Injectivity] if $w\in\mathbb C^3$ and $\operatorname{Re}(we^{-i\omega t})=0$ for all $t\in\mathbb R$, then $w=0$; more generally, if $w:D\to\mathbb C^3$ is continuous and $\operatorname{Re}(w(x)e^{-i\omega t})=0$ for all $(x,t)\in D\times\mathbb R$, then $w\equiv0$ on $D$. (c) [Equivalence] if $\widetilde E,\widetilde B$ are $C^1$, the phasor system $$\operatorname{div}\widetilde E=0,\quad\operatorname{div}\widetilde B=0,\quad\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=i\omega\widetilde B,\quad\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E$$ holds on $D$ if and only if the real system $$\operatorname{div}E=0,\quad\operatorname{div}B=0,\quad\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\quad\operatorname{curl}B=c^{-2}\partial_tE$$ holds on $D\times\mathbb R$.
before.strategy: Write the encoding in real components: by the Cartesian form and Euler identity of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], $\operatorname{Re}(w(x)e^{-i\omega t})=(\operatorname{Re}w(x))\cos(\omega t)+(\operatorname{Im}w(x))\sin(\omega t)$ componentwise, with the real and imaginary parts of [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]] and the complex arithmetic of [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. (a) For fixed $x$ each component is a constant-coefficient combination of $\cos(\omega t)$ and $\sin(\omega t)$; the sum, scalar-multiple and product rules of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] with the derivatives of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] give $\partial_tE=\operatorname{Re}(-i\omega\widetilde Ee^{-i\omega t})$, and the spatial derivatives pass through the constant coefficients, giving the spatial formulas for each component; the divergence and curl formulas follow by applying the componentwise formulas and the linearity of [[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]] (for complex fields, componentwise in real and imaginary parts). (b) Evaluating at $t=0$ gives $\operatorname{Re}w=0$; evaluating at $t=\pi/(2\omega)$ gives $\operatorname{Re}(-iw)=\operatorname{Im}w=0$ by the quarter-turn values of [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]] and the Cartesian form of [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], so $w=0$. The continuous case applies the pointwise result at each $x\in D$; no choice principle is used. (c) Direction (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii): substitute the phasor equations into the calculus formulas of (a); e.g. $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E)e^{-i\omega t})=\operatorname{Re}(i\omega\widetilde Be^{-i\omega t})=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\operatorname{Re}(-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde Ee^{-i\omega t})=c^{-2}\partial_tE$. Direction (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i): subtract the complex expressions and apply (b), e.g. $\operatorname{Re}((\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E-i\omega\widetilde B)e^{-i\omega t})=0$ for all $(x,t)$ forces $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E=i\omega\widetilde B$; the other three equations are analogous. All statements are pointwise algebraic identities; no PDE existence, no boundary condition and no choice principle is used.

before.title: Adopted scalar aperture-diffraction model (polarization-insensitive regime)
before.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] and [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] ([[def-countable-choice]]); the smooth modal full-Choice branch of the latter is not used. Adopt as a model assumption of the framework the following scalar aperture-diffraction model. [Data] Fix an angular frequency $\omega>0$ and wavenumber $k:=\omega/c$, with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $S\subset\{y\in\mathbb R^3:y_3=0\}\cap B_a(0)$ be a nonempty compact subset of a declared aperture plane $y_3=0$ with aperture radius $a>0$ (the screening plane and spatial region are read in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]), and let $\alpha$ be a finite complex measure on $\mathbb R^3$ supported in $S$ (the **aperture distribution**), with $\alpha$ read in volts so that the model field below carries the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ of an electric-field component and its pairings are those of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. [Model field] The model assigns to every observation point $x$ with $x_3>0$ the complex scalar amplitude $$u(x):=\int G_k(x-y)\,d\alpha(y),$$ where $G_k(z)=e^{ik|z|}/(4\pi|z|)$ for $z\ne0$ is the outgoing Helmholtz kernel of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], together with the real scalar field $U(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and the model period-averaged squared field $(1/2)|u(x)|^2$. All model predictions are declared comparisons of this squared field between observation points; no absolute radiometric power or intensity calibration is adopted. [Adopted regime and status] The model is the declared polarization-insensitive scalar approximation of aperture diffraction. It ignores the vector nature and polarization of the electromagnetic field, takes the aperture distribution rather than the exact screen traces as its datum, assigns no back-reaction of the diffracted field on the illumination and no screen interaction beyond the aperture, and is not derived from either branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] or from the material-closure branches of [[post-em-material-closure]]; it is a declared optical approximation, not an exact electromagnetic model. It does not assert that $u$ or $U$ satisfies the Maxwell equations exactly, and it does not identify $\alpha$ with the unknown exact Maxwell boundary traces: assigning both $u$ and $\partial_nu$ on the aperture independently is not a well-posed exact boundary problem, as recorded in [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]], and the error terms of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] are the controlled content of the model. No measured intensity, apparatus, sampling model, uncertainty budget, empirical comparison or quantitative radiometric calibration is adopted.
before.strategy: This is an explicit adopted-assumption contract; it is deliberately not a derivation. (i) The mathematical object it adopts is the outgoing source field $u=G_k*\alpha$ of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], whose kernel, support class and outgoing/Fraunhofer error terms are fixed there; the integral against the finite complex measure is that of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. (ii) The physical reading uses the aperture plane and spatial region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], the wavenumber-frequency relation $k=\omega/c$ and the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (iii) The non-derivation clause is essential: neither the smooth nor the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] implies this scalar source model, and the finite-conductivity/material branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] contain no ideal aperture or screen model; the trace caveat is the one recorded in [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]]. (iv) The scope sentences exclude exact Maxwell, vector, polarization, back-reaction, absolute-radiometric and empirical content. The item uses no choice principle beyond those carried by the cited mathematical suppliers (the kernel lemma carries Countable Choice, as stated there). The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited verbatim from the cited kernel and boundary-representation suppliers; this postulate adds no choice use of its own.

[Data] Fix an angular frequency $\omega>0$ and wavenumber $k:=\omega/c$, with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $S\subset\{y\in\mathbb R^3:y_3=0\}\cap\{y:|y|\le a\}$ be a nonempty compact subset of a declared aperture plane $y_3=0$ with aperture radius $a>0$ (the screening plane and spatial region are read in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]), and let $\alpha$ be a finite complex measure on $\mathbb R^3$ supported in $S$ (the **aperture distribution**), with $\alpha$ read in volts so that the model field below carries the unit $\mathrm V\,\mathrm m^{-1}$ of an electric-field component and its pairings are those of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. [Model field] The model assigns to every observation point $x$ with $x_3>0$ the complex scalar amplitude $$u(x):=\int G_k(x-y)\,d\alpha(y),$$ where $G_k(z)=e^{ik|z|}/(4\pi|z|)$ for $z\ne0$ is the outgoing Helmholtz kernel of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], together with the real scalar field $U(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and the model period-averaged squared field $(1/2)|u(x)|^2$. All model predictions are declared comparisons of this squared field between observation points; no absolute radiometric power or intensity calibration is adopted. [Adopted regime and status] The model is the declared polarization-insensitive scalar approximation of aperture diffraction. It ignores the vector nature and polarization of the electromagnetic field, takes the aperture distribution rather than the exact screen traces as its datum, assigns no back-reaction of the diffracted field on the illumination and no screen interaction beyond the aperture, and is not derived from either branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] or from the material-closure branches of [[post-em-material-closure]]; it is a declared optical approximation, not an exact electromagnetic model. It does not assert that $u$ or $U$ satisfies the Maxwell equations exactly, and it does not identify $\alpha$ with the unknown exact Maxwell boundary traces: assigning both $u$ and $\partial_nu$ on the aperture independently is not a well-posed exact boundary problem, as recorded in [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]], and the error terms of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] are the controlled content of the model. No measured intensity, apparatus, sampling model, uncertainty budget, empirical comparison or quantitative radiometric calibration is adopted.
after.strategy: This is an explicit adopted-assumption contract; it is deliberately not a derivation. (i) The mathematical object it adopts is the outgoing source field $u=G_k*\alpha$ of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]], whose kernel and outgoing/Fraunhofer technique are fixed there. This model permits the compact closed-radius support $|y|\le a$, including aperture corners. Its integral and off-support regularity fall under that supplier by choosing any containing open ball of radius $A>a$; the sharp-radius estimates at $r\ge2a$ are proved directly in the consuming diffraction theorem, so this extension does not evaluate an open-support hypothesis at a boundary point; the integral against the finite complex measure is that of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. (ii) The physical reading uses the aperture plane and spatial region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], the wavenumber-frequency relation $k=\omega/c$ and the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (iii) The non-derivation clause is essential: neither the smooth nor the weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] implies this scalar source model, and the finite-conductivity/material branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] contain no ideal aperture or screen model; the trace caveat is the one recorded in [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]]. (iv) The scope sentences exclude exact Maxwell, vector, polarization, back-reaction, absolute-radiometric and empirical content. The item uses no choice principle beyond those carried by the cited mathematical suppliers (the kernel lemma carries Countable Choice, as stated there). The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited verbatim from the cited kernel and boundary-representation suppliers; this postulate adds no choice use of its own.

before.title: Controlled scalar aperture diffraction: Fresnel and Fraunhofer approximations with explicit error terms
before.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] and [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] ([[def-countable-choice]]), whose trace qualification is used in clause (d); the full-Choice modal branch of the latter is not used. Adopt the scalar aperture model and its notation from [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]]: frequency $\omega>0$, $k=\omega/c$, aperture radius $a>0$, finite complex aperture distribution $\alpha$ supported in the planar aperture $S\subset\{y_3=0\}\cap B_a(0)$, model field $u=G_k*\alpha$, real field $U(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and $T=2\pi/\omega$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-complex-exponential]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]). Set $I(x):=(1/2)|u(x)|^2$. Then: (a) [Model field and Fraunhofer estimate] $u$ is $C^\infty$ on the half-space $\{x_3>0\}$ and on $\mathbb R^3\setminus S$, satisfies $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ there, and is outgoing in the sense of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]]: for $x=rn$ with $r\ge2a$ and $n\in S^2$, $$u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)+O\Bigl(\frac{\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}}{r}\Bigl[\frac ar+\frac{ka^2}{r}\Bigr]\Bigr)$$ uniformly in direction, and $r(\partial_ru-iku)=O(r^{-1})$ uniformly. (b) [Fresnel estimate] for the planar aperture and observation $x=(\xi_1,\xi_2,z)$ with $z>0$, $|\xi|\le b$ and $a+b\ll z$, the Fresnel approximation replaces $R=|x-y|$ by $z+|\xi-y|^2/(2z)$ and $1/R$ by $1/z$ in the model integral with phase error $O(k(a+b)^4/z^3)$, relative amplitude error $O((a+b)^2/z^2)$ and absolute field error $O(\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}z^{-1}[(a+b)^2/z^2+k(a+b)^4/z^3])$. (c) [Intensity and error transfer] at every $x$ with $x_3>0$ the model period average satisfies $\frac1T\int_0^TU(x,s)^2\,ds=I(x)$ ([[lem-em-period-average]]). If $u_{\rm approx}$ is any approximation of $u$ with $|u_{\rm approx}(x)-u(x)|\le\delta(x)$, then $|\frac12|u_{\rm approx}(x)|^2-I(x)|\le\frac12\delta(x)(|u(x)|+|u_{\rm approx}(x)|)$; if moreover $u(x)\ne0$ and $|u_{\rm approx}(x)-u(x)|\le\epsilon(x)|u(x)|$, the relative intensity error is at most $2\epsilon(x)+\epsilon(x)^2$. In particular the Fraunhofer and Fresnel field errors of (a) and (b) bound the corresponding intensity errors; no new approximation is introduced by passing to $I$. (d) [Trace and scope] the aperture distribution $\alpha$ is an adopted model datum and is not identified with the exact Maxwell boundary data on the screen; assigning both $u$ and $\partial_nu$ on the aperture independently does not produce a well-posed exact boundary problem ([[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]]). The construction ignores polarization and aperture back-reaction, makes no claim that $u$ or $U$ satisfies the Maxwell equations exactly, and makes no measured-intensity, apparatus, sampling or empirical claim; only comparisons of $I$ between observation points are read as model predictions.
before.strategy: The theorem instantiates the mathematical field estimates of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] at the adopted model datum of [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]]. (a) is exactly the supplier's statement for $u=G_k*\alpha$ with $\alpha$ supported in $B_a(0)$ intersected with the aperture plane, including the uniform Fraunhofer error, the outgoing residual and the off-support smoothness; no re-derivation is needed because the model field is defined to be that supplier's field. (b) is the supplier's planar-aperture Fresnel estimate, whose phase and amplitude errors are Taylor-remainder bounds for $R=|x-y|$ on the compact small-$s$ region $s=|\xi-y|^2/z^2$; the same estimates apply to the model because the datum is the same finite complex measure. (c) applies [[lem-em-period-average]] with $a=d=u(x)$: $\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})^2$ averages to $\frac12\operatorname{Re}(u(x)\overline{u(x)})=\frac12|u(x)|^2$. The first error bound is the identity $\frac12||u_{\rm approx}|^2-|u|^2|=\frac12|u_{\rm approx}-u|\,||u_{\rm approx}|+|u||$ together with $||u_{\rm approx}|-|u||\le|u_{\rm approx}-u|$; the relative bound is $||u_{\rm approx}|^2-|u|^2|/|u|^2\le\epsilon(2+\epsilon)$. No choice principle beyond that carried by the suppliers is used. (d) reproduces the trace distinction of [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] and the model-scope declarations of the postulate; the intensity reading is the declared one, so no radiometric claim is added. The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited from the cited suppliers; the intensity computation of (c) uses only the choice-free period-average lemma.

after.strategy: The theorem instantiates the mathematical field estimates of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] at the adopted model datum of [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]]. (a) The model field is the supplier's convolution. Choose any open containing ball of radius $A>a$ to obtain its off-support smoothness and Helmholtz equation. For the advertised sharp-radius endpoint, argue directly for every $|y|\le a$ and $r\ge2a$. Write $R=|rn-y|$, so $R\ge r-a\ge r/2$. For $h(s)=|rn-sy|$, the exact norm derivative formula from the supplier gives $|h''(s)|\le2a^2/(r-a)\le4a^2/r$; twice FTC therefore gives $|R-r+n\cdot y|\le2a^2/r$, and $|r/R-1|\le2a/r$. The supplier's real phase bound $|e^{i\theta}-1|\le|\theta|$ now gives $$\left|G_k(rn-y)-\frac{e^{ikr}e^{-ikn\cdot y}}{4\pi r}\right|\le\frac1{2\pi r}\left(\frac ar+\frac{ka^2}r\right).$$ For a bounded continuous kernel $f$ on the compact support, $|\int f\,d\alpha|\le\sup|f|\,\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}$ follows by [[prop-simple-integrals-are-bounded-by-total-variation]] and uniform finite-simple approximation in [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]; hence this pointwise bound proves the original field error, including $r=2a$. The exact derivative $\partial_rR=(r-n\cdot y)/R$ has modulus at most1 and $|\partial_rR-1|\le2a^2/r^2$. Differentiating the explicit kernel gives $r|\partial_rG_k-ikG_k|\le(\pi r)^{-1}(1+ka^2/r)$; the same finite-measure bound gives the uniform outgoing residual. All derivative passages under the source integral use the supplier's compact-product uniform difference-quotient argument, not an unsupported complex-measure dominated-convergence claim. (b) On the explicitly declared range put $d_0=a+b$ and $s=|\xi-y_t|^2/z^2\le\eta_0^2<1$. The actual supplier proof gives $|\sqrt{1+s}-1-s/2|\le s^2/8$ and $|(1+s)^{-1/2}-1|\le s/2$ by twice FTC. Consequently the phase error is at most $kd_0^4/(8z^3)$ and the relative amplitude error at most $d_0^2/(2z^2)$. The complex-measure kernel bound above gives $$|u-u_{\rm Fresnel}|\le\frac{\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}}{4\pi z}\left[\frac{d_0^2}{2z^2}+\frac{kd_0^4}{8z^3}\right],$$ which preserves and quantifies all original Fresnel estimates for the closed-support datum. (c) applies [[lem-em-period-average]] with $a=d=u(x)$: $\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})^2$ averages to $\frac12\operatorname{Re}(u(x)\overline{u(x)})=\frac12|u(x)|^2$. The first error bound is the identity $\frac12\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|^2-|u|^2\bigr|=\frac12\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|-|u|\bigr|(|u_{\rm approx}|+|u|)$ together with $\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|-|u|\bigr|\le|u_{\rm approx}-u|$, obtained by applying the triangle inequality of [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]] in both directions; the relative bound is $||u_{\rm approx}|^2-|u|^2|/|u|^2\le\epsilon(2+\epsilon)$. No choice principle beyond that carried by the suppliers is used. (d) reproduces the trace distinction of [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] and the model-scope declarations of the postulate; the intensity reading is the declared one, so no radiometric claim is added. The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited from the cited suppliers; the intensity computation of (c) uses only the choice-free period-average lemma.

before.title: Monochromatic scattering by a smooth perfect-electric-conductor obstacle
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as carried by [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]], whose variational, Sobolev-compactness and compact-spectral steps use it; the algebraic computations below use no further choice. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary, $D:=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ connected, $k>0$, $\omega:=ck$ with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$; let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open with $\overline D\subseteq V$, and let $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc},\widetilde B_{\rm inc})$ be a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on $V$ ([[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Plane-wave instances are provided by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]]: if $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$ and $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, then $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc},\widetilde B_{\rm inc})(x)=(e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x},b\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x})$ satisfies the four phasor equations on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]). Adopt the ideal perfectly conducting (PEC) boundary model: the tangential component of the total electric field vanishes on $\partial O$. This is a declared idealization of the stationary interface conditions of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] with vanishing fields inside the conductor; it is not one of the finite-conductivity branches of [[post-em-material-closure]], and the induced surface charge and current are neither prescribed nor determined here. Let $e_T$ be the tangential projection of $-\widetilde E_{\rm inc}$ on $\partial O$, and let $\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ be the unique $C^\infty$ field on $\overline D$ of [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] with $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ and $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ on $D$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$ and that lemma's outgoing modal condition on $S_R$. Set $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}:=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ and, on $D$, $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}:=\widetilde E_{\rm inc}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$, $\widetilde B_{\rm tot}:=\widetilde B_{\rm inc}+\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$. Then: (a) [Phasor Maxwell] $(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ and $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ are $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pairs on $D$; and for every $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair $(\widetilde E,\widetilde B)$ on an open set $O'\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, the associated real fields of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]] satisfy on $O'\times\mathbb R$ the smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho\equiv0$ and $J\equiv0$. Consequently the associated real total fields $E_{\rm tot},B_{\rm tot}$ satisfy those source-free equations on $D\times\mathbb R$. (b) [PEC boundary condition] the tangential trace of $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}$ on $\partial O$ vanishes; hence for every unit normal field $n$ of $\partial O$ the associated real total electric field $E_{\rm tot}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E_{\rm tot}(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) satisfies $n\times E_{\rm tot}=0$ on $\partial O\times\mathbb R$. (c) [Uniqueness] if $(\widetilde E',\widetilde B')$ is a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on an open set $V'\supseteq\overline D$ that is outgoing on $S_R$ in the modal sense of the vector Helmholtz lemma and has tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$, then $(\widetilde E',\widetilde B')=(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ on $D$; equivalently $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ is the unique outgoing total pair with the prescribed incident phasor and $n\times E_{\rm tot}=0$ on $\partial O$. (d) [Scope] one positive frequency $\omega=ck$, one smooth bounded stationary PEC obstacle with connected exterior, and $C^\infty$ incident and scattered classes only; no lossy, impedance, nonsmooth or dispersive obstacle, no determination of the induced surface charge or current, no radiation-zone amplitude or far-field asymptotics beyond the lemma's outgoing modal class, no point or singular source, no finite-energy or empirical claim.
before.strategy: Assume the Axiom of Choice exactly through [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] (its symmetry/coercivity, compactness and compact-spectral steps); all other steps are pointwise algebra. (a) For the scattered pair: $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ is the boundary-problem condition; $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=i\omega\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ holds by the definition of $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$; $\operatorname{div}\widetilde B_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}(\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=(i\omega)^{-1}(\nabla\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}-\Delta\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=(i\omega)^{-1}k^2\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ by [[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]], [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$; the sum of two solutions of the linear system is a solution by [[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]. The real-field Maxwell statement is clause (c) of [[lem-em-phasor-real-part-calculus-and-equivalence]] with the constant $c$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]], combined with the identification of its real system with the zero-source smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; the incident pair is a pair on $V$, hence on $D$. (b) The tangential traces satisfy $\widetilde E_{\rm tot,tang}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat,tang}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+e_T=0$ on $\partial O$; the associated real field is the real part of the tangential trace, hence vanishes (the encoding and real-part calculus are those of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]] and [[lem-em-phasor-real-part-calculus-and-equivalence]]). (c) A candidate $\widetilde E'$ of the stated class satisfies all hypotheses of the uniqueness assertion of [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] for the same tangential data, so $\widetilde E'=\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$; then $\widetilde B'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ by the third phasor equation of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]]. (d) records the exact scope; in particular the ideal PEC condition is adopted, not derived, and the material-closure branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] contain no $\sigma\to\infty$ branch, while [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] supplies only the stationary-interface idealization context.

before.physical_scope: Conditional vector scattering of a smooth frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair by a smooth bounded stationary perfect electric conductor with connected exterior: the scattered and total phasor pairs, the associated real fields solving the zero-source smooth vacuum Maxwell equations on the exterior, the ideal PEC boundary condition $n\times E_{\rm tot}=0$, and uniqueness of the outgoing scattered solution with the prescribed tangential trace. Excluded: lossy, impedance, nonsmooth or dispersive obstacles; determination of induced surface charge or current; radiation-zone amplitude asymptotics beyond the outgoing modal class; singular or point sources; finite-energy, coupled self-force and every empirical claim.

after.title: Monochromatic scattering by a smooth perfect-electric-conductor obstacle
after.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as carried by [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]], whose variational, Sobolev-compactness and compact-spectral steps use it; the algebraic computations below use no further choice. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary, $D:=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ connected, $k>0$, $\omega:=ck$ with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$; let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open with $\overline D\subseteq V$, and let $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc},\widetilde B_{\rm inc})$ be a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on $V$ ([[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Plane-wave instances are provided by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]]: if $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$ and $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, then $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc},\widetilde B_{\rm inc})(x)=(e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x},b\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x})$ satisfies the four phasor equations on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]). Adopt the ideal perfectly conducting (PEC) boundary model: the tangential component of the total electric field vanishes on $\partial O$. This is a declared idealization of the stationary interface conditions of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] with vanishing fields inside the conductor; it is not one of the finite-conductivity branches of [[post-em-material-closure]], and the induced surface charge and current are neither prescribed nor determined here. Let $e_T$ be the tangential projection of $-\widetilde E_{\rm inc}$ on $\partial O$, and let $\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ be the unique $C^\infty$ field on $\overline D$ of [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] with $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ and $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ on $D$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$ and that lemma's outgoing modal condition on $S_R$. Set $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}:=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ and, on $D$, $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}:=\widetilde E_{\rm inc}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$, $\widetilde B_{\rm tot}:=\widetilde B_{\rm inc}+\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$. Then: (a) [Phasor Maxwell] $(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ and $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ are $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pairs on $D$; and for every $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair $(\widetilde E,\widetilde B)$ on an open set $O'\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, the associated real fields of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]] satisfy on $O'\times\mathbb R$ the smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho\equiv0$ and $J\equiv0$. Consequently the associated real total fields $E_{\rm tot},B_{\rm tot}$ satisfy those source-free equations on $D\times\mathbb R$. (b) [PEC boundary condition] the tangential trace of $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}$ on $\partial O$ vanishes; hence for every unit normal field $n$ of $\partial O$ the associated real total electric field $E_{\rm tot}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E_{\rm tot}(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) satisfies $n\times E_{\rm tot}=0$ on $\partial O\times\mathbb R$. (c) [Uniqueness] if $(\widetilde E',\widetilde B')$ is a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on an open set $V'\supseteq\overline D$ that is outgoing on $S_R$ in the modal sense of the vector Helmholtz lemma and has tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$, then $(\widetilde E',\widetilde B')=(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ on $D$; equivalently $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ is the unique total source-free phasor pair in the corresponding $C^\infty$ closure class with that prescribed incident phasor, vanishing tangential electric trace, and outgoing scattered correction $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}-\widetilde E_{\rm inc}$ in the lemma's modal class. The total field itself is not required to be outgoing; an incident plane wave is generally not outgoing. (d) [Scope] one positive frequency $\omega=ck$, one smooth bounded stationary PEC obstacle with connected exterior, and $C^\infty$ incident and scattered classes only; no lossy, impedance, nonsmooth or dispersive obstacle, no determination of the induced surface charge or current, no radiation-zone amplitude or far-field asymptotics beyond the lemma's outgoing modal class, no point or singular source, no finite-energy or empirical claim.
after.strategy: Assume the Axiom of Choice exactly through [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] (its symmetry/coercivity, compactness and compact-spectral steps); all other steps are pointwise algebra. (a) For the scattered pair: $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ is the boundary-problem condition; $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=i\omega\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ holds by the definition of $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$; $\operatorname{div}\widetilde B_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}(\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=(i\omega)^{-1}(\nabla\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}-\Delta\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=(i\omega)^{-1}k^2\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ by [[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]], [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$; the sum of two solutions of the linear system is a solution by [[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]. The real-field Maxwell statement is clause (c) of [[lem-em-phasor-real-part-calculus-and-equivalence]] with the constant $c$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]], combined with the identification of its real system with the zero-source smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; the incident pair is a pair on $V$, hence on $D$. (b) The tangential traces satisfy $\widetilde E_{\rm tot,tang}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat,tang}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+e_T=0$ on $\partial O$; the associated real field is the real part of the tangential trace, hence vanishes (the encoding and real-part calculus are those of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]] and [[lem-em-phasor-real-part-calculus-and-equivalence]]). (c) For a candidate phasor pair, $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E'=i\omega\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B'=\omega^2c^{-2}\widetilde E'=k^2\widetilde E'$, and $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E'=0$. The componentwise real/imaginary curl-curl identity thus gives $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E'=0$. Its prescribed tangential trace and outgoing correction are the declared boundary class. Hence the candidate $\widetilde E'$ satisfies all hypotheses of the uniqueness assertion of [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] for the same tangential data, so $\widetilde E'=\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$; then $\widetilde B'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ by the third phasor equation of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]]. For the total-field formulation subtract the fixed incident pair: linearity gives a source-free correction with tangential trace $e_T$, and the required outgoing condition is on that correction. Conversely adding the fixed incident pair recovers the total boundary condition. Thus uniqueness transfers exactly to total-minus-incident outgoing; it does not impose the outgoing class on an incident plane wave or on their total. (d) records the exact scope; in particular the ideal PEC condition is adopted, not derived, and the material-closure branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] contain no $\sigma\to\infty$ branch, while [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] supplies only the stationary-interface idealization context.

before.title: Uniform rectangular aperture: the Fraunhofer sinc-squared pattern
before.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]] and by the Riemann-Lebesgue comparison and Fubini suppliers used in the integral reduction below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the scalar aperture model of [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]] and [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]], with frequency $\omega>0$, $k=\omega/c$, aperture plane $y_3=0$, model field $u=G_k*\alpha$ and $I(x)=\frac12|u(x)|^2$. Fix $a>0$, $b>0$ and $A_0\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$; identify the rectangle $R:=[-a,a]\times[-b,b]\subset\mathbb R^2$ with the planar aperture $\{(y_1,y_2,0):(y_1,y_2)\in R\}$ and take the **uniform rectangular aperture distribution** $$\alpha:=A_0\,\lambda_R,\qquad \alpha(E):=A_0\,\lambda_2(E\cap R)\ \text{ for Borel } E\subseteq\mathbb R^2,$$ the finite complex measure of constant density $A_0$ on $R$ with respect to the two-dimensional Lebesgue measure $\lambda_2$ ([[def-multidimensional-rectangle-and-volume]], [[def-measure-with-density]], [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]). Then: (a) [Fraunhofer amplitude] with $\operatorname{sinc}\xi:=\sin\xi/\xi$ for $\xi\ne0$ and $\operatorname{sinc}0:=1$, the Fraunhofer amplitude factor of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a) is exactly $$\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)=4abA_0\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)\qquad(n=(n_1,n_2,n_3)\in S^2),$$ an identity for every direction $n$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-complex-exponential]], [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]], [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]). (b) [Fraunhofer intensity] in the Fraunhofer regime of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a) with aperture radius $a':=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, i.e. for $r\ge2a'$, the model intensity is $$I_{\rm F}(rn)=\frac{a^2b^2|A_0|^2}{2\pi^2r^2}\operatorname{sinc}^2(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}^2(kb\,n_2)$$ up to the Fraunhofer absolute error of that theorem, transferred to $I$ by its clause (c). The pattern vanishes exactly where $ka\,n_1\in\pi\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ or $kb\,n_2\in\pi\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, and has its central maximum at $n=(0,0,\pm1)$. (c) [Scope] this is an exact computation inside the adopted ideal scalar model, not a measured diffraction record: no absolute radiometric calibration, polarization content, screen interaction, apparatus model or sampling law is asserted, and the Fraunhofer/Fresnel error bounds of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]] are inherited rather than re-estimated.
before.strategy: (a) Because $\alpha=A_0\lambda_R$ has density $A_0$ with respect to $\lambda_2$ on $R$, [[def-measure-with-density]] and [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]] give $\int f\,d\alpha=A_0\int_Rf\,d\lambda_2$ for every bounded Borel $f$ (apply the identity to the positive density $|A_0|$ and multiply by the unimodular factor $A_0/|A_0|$, with real and imaginary parts by [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]). For $f(y)=e^{-ik(n_1y_1+n_2y_2)}$ (the $y_3$-coordinate is zero on the aperture, and $n\cdot y=n_1y_1+n_2y_2$ by [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), $f$ is continuous on the compact rectangle $R$ ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]), so [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] identifies the Lebesgue integral with the Riemann double integral; [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] factors it into the product of the two one-dimensional integrals. For $\xi\ne0$, the one-dimensional integral is $\int_{-a}^aI_0\,e^{-ikn_1y_1}\,dy_1=2\sin(ka\,n_1)/(kn_1)=2a\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)$ by [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] applied to the real and imaginary parts via [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]; for $n_1=0$ it equals $2a=2a\operatorname{sinc}0$ by the defining limit value, so the formula holds for every direction. The second factor is analogous, giving the displayed product $4abA_0\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)$. (b) Insert the product amplitude into the Fraunhofer expression $u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}d\alpha(y)+$error of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a), square the modulus and use $I=\frac12|u|^2$; the modulus of the amplitude is $4ab|A_0||\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)||\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)|$, so $|u_{\rm F}|^2=\frac{a^2b^2|A_0|^2}{\pi^2r^2}\operatorname{sinc}^2(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}^2(kb\,n_2)$ and the factor $\frac12$ gives the displayed $I_{\rm F}$. The vanishing/central-maximum reading is the elementary zero set of $\xi\mapsto\sin\xi/\xi$: $\operatorname{sinc}\xi=0$ exactly for $\xi\in\pi\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, and $|\operatorname{sinc}\xi|\le1$ with equality at $\xi=0$ away from those zeros. The support of $\alpha$ lies in $B_{a'}(0)$ with $a'=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, so the theorem's Fraunhofer condition $r\ge2a$ is met at $r\ge2a'$; clause (c) of the theorem transfers the field error to $I$. (c) is the scope of the model; no additional approximation is introduced. The computation uses only the standard Riemann/Lebesgue and trigonometric suppliers listed in the dependencies; the Countable Choice assumption is exactly the one carried by the Riemann-Lebesgue comparison and Fubini interfaces, with no additional choice.

after.title: Uniform rectangular aperture: the Fraunhofer sinc-squared pattern
after.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]] and by the Riemann-Lebesgue comparison and Fubini suppliers used in the integral reduction below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the scalar aperture model of [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]] and [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]], with frequency $\omega>0$, $k=\omega/c$, aperture plane $y_3=0$, model field $u=G_k*\alpha$ and $I(x)=\frac12|u(x)|^2$. Fix $a>0$, $b>0$ and $A_0\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$; identify the rectangle $R:=[-a,a]\times[-b,b]\subset\mathbb R^2$ with the planar aperture $\{(y_1,y_2,0):(y_1,y_2)\in R\}$ and take the **uniform rectangular aperture distribution** let $\iota:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^3$ be $\iota(y_1,y_2)=(y_1,y_2,0)$, and define its plane-embedding pushforward $$\alpha(E):=A_0\,\lambda_2(R\cap\iota^{-1}(E))\qquad(E\subseteq\mathbb R^3\text{ Borel}).$$ This is a finite complex measure on $\mathbb R^3$, supported on the embedded compact rectangle $S=\iota(R)$ with $|y|\le a':=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$ and total variation $\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}=4ab|A_0|$ ([[def-multidimensional-rectangle-and-volume]], [[def-measure-with-density]], [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]). Then: (a) [Fraunhofer amplitude] with $\operatorname{sinc}\xi:=\sin\xi/\xi$ for $\xi\ne0$ and $\operatorname{sinc}0:=1$, the Fraunhofer amplitude factor of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a) is exactly $$\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)=4abA_0\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)\qquad(n=(n_1,n_2,n_3)\in S^2),$$ an identity for every direction $n$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-complex-exponential]], [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]], [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]). (b) [Fraunhofer intensity] in the Fraunhofer regime of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a) with aperture radius $a':=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, i.e. for $r\ge2a'$, the model intensity is $$I_{\rm F}(rn)=\frac{a^2b^2|A_0|^2}{2\pi^2r^2}\operatorname{sinc}^2(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}^2(kb\,n_2)$$ up to the Fraunhofer absolute error of that theorem, transferred to $I$ by its clause (c). The pattern vanishes exactly where $ka\,n_1\in\pi\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ or $kb\,n_2\in\pi\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, and, as a mathematical pattern on all $S^2$, has its global maximum exactly at the two poles $n=(0,0,\pm1)$. The model observes only $x_3>0$; its allowed directions have $n_3>0$, where the central maximum is only $n=(0,0,1)$. (c) [Scope] this is an exact computation inside the adopted ideal scalar model, not a measured diffraction record: no absolute radiometric calibration, polarization content, screen interaction, apparatus model or sampling law is asserted, and the Fraunhofer/Fresnel error bounds of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]] are inherited rather than re-estimated.
after.strategy: (a) The continuous embedding $\iota$ has Borel inverse images by [[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]. Disjoint Borel sets have disjoint inverse images; countable additivity of $\lambda_2$ therefore proves directly that the displayed $\alpha$ is a complex measure as in [[def-complex-measure]]. It is supported on $S=\iota(R)$. For every countable partition, the sum of the moduli of its values is $|A_0|\lambda_2(R)=4ab|A_0|$ by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], so [[def-total-variation-of-a-signed-or-complex-measure]] gives the stated finite total variation. For a simple Borel $f$ on $\mathbb R^3$ the defining sum gives $\int f\,d\alpha=A_0\int_Rf(\iota(y))\,d\lambda_2(y)$; uniform finite-simple approximations of any bounded Borel $f$ and the total-variation bound pass this identity to the integrals of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. Thus the plane measure is correctly typed for the three-dimensional model. For $f(y)=e^{-ik(n_1y_1+n_2y_2)}$ (the $y_3$-coordinate is zero on the aperture, and $n\cdot y=n_1y_1+n_2y_2$ by [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), $f$ is continuous on the compact rectangle $R$ ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]), so [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] identifies the Lebesgue integral with the Riemann double integral; [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] factors it into the product of the two one-dimensional integrals. For $n_1\ne0$, the one-dimensional integral is $\int_{-a}^a e^{-ikn_1y_1}\,dy_1=2\sin(ka\,n_1)/(kn_1)=2a\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)$ by [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] for the affine phase $y_1\mapsto-kn_1y_1$, applied to the real and imaginary parts via [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]; for $n_1=0$ it equals $2a=2a\operatorname{sinc}0$ by the separately defined value, so the formula holds for every direction. The second factor is analogous, giving the displayed product $4abA_0\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)$. (b) Insert the product amplitude into the Fraunhofer expression $u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}d\alpha(y)+$error of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a), square the modulus and use $I=\frac12|u|^2$; the modulus of the amplitude is $4ab|A_0||\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)||\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)|$, so $|u_{\rm F}|^2=\frac{a^2b^2|A_0|^2}{\pi^2r^2}\operatorname{sinc}^2(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}^2(kb\,n_2)$ and the factor $\frac12$ gives the displayed $I_{\rm F}$. The zero assertion follows from [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]] and the separate value at0. To prove the exact maxima, $|\sin x|<|x|$ for every $x\ne0$: for $x>0$ set $\delta=\min\{x/3,\pi/6\}>0$. On $[\delta,2\delta]$, the cosine signs and strict monotonicity of [[thm-sine-cosine-signs-monotonicity-and-ranges]] give $|\cos t|\le\cos\delta<1$, while globally $|\cos t|\le1$. FTC and the Riemann integral triangle/monotonicity estimate (applied to $-|\cos|\le\cos\le|\cos|$) give $|\sin x|\le\int_0^x|\cos t|\,dt\le x-\delta(1-\cos\delta)<x$; continuous integrability and subinterval additivity are supplied by [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]] and [[thm-additivity-over-subintervals]]. Negative $x$ follows from sine oddness in [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]. Thus $|\operatorname{sinc}x|=1$ exactly at0, and since $k,a,b>0$ the product attains its maximum exactly when $n_1=n_2=0$, the two spherical poles. Only the positive pole belongs to the model upper half-space. The embedded corners have norm exactly $a'=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$; the support lies in the closed radius set $|y|\le a'$, so the parent theorem's directly proved closed-support estimate applies at the unchanged endpoint $r\ge2a'$; clause (c) of the theorem transfers the field error to $I$. (c) is the scope of the model; no additional approximation is introduced. The computation uses only the standard Riemann/Lebesgue and trigonometric suppliers listed in the dependencies; the Countable Choice assumption is exactly the one carried by the Riemann-Lebesgue comparison and Fubini interfaces, with no additional choice.

## Statement

For real $x,y$, $\exp(x+iy)=e^x(\cos y+i\sin y)$ and $|\exp(x+iy)|=e^x$. In particular $e^{i\pi}+1=0$. The conventions and prerequisite facts used below are recorded in [[thm-complex-exponential-addition-and-real-extension]], [[thm-eulers-formula]], [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]], [[thm-pythagorean-and-parity-identities-for-all-six-trigonometric-functions]], [[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-quarter-turn-values-and-shift-formulas]], [[def-pi-via-first-positive-cosine-zero]].

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Reals $x,y$.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Apply the addition law to $x+iy$ and Euler's formula. [given]

1.2 Multiplicativity of modulus, the Pythagorean identity, and positivity of $e^x$ give the modulus formula. [given]

2.1 The defining quarter-turn value $\cos\pi=-1$ and $\sin\pi=0$ give Euler's identity. [given] ∎

## Statement

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^2$. Then $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}F$, $\nabla\operatorname{div}F$ and $\Delta F$ are all defined on $U$ and

$$\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}F=\nabla\operatorname{div}F-\Delta F.$$

Here $\Delta F$ is the componentwise Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]].

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ and the $C^2$ field $F:U\to\mathbb R^3$ of the Statement, with the three coordinates named $x,y,z$.

[F1] The curl of a $C^1$ field $F$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ is $\operatorname{curl}F=(\partial_yF_z-\partial_zF_y,\ \partial_zF_x-\partial_xF_z,\ \partial_xF_y-\partial_yF_x)$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]).

[F2] The divergence of a $C^1$ field $G$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is $\operatorname{div}G=\sum_{i<n}\partial_iG_i$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]).

[F3] For a $C^2$ map $F$, $\Delta F$ is the field whose $i$th coordinate is $\Delta F_i$, and $\Delta f=\sum_{i<n}\partial_i\partial_if$ for a $C^2$ scalar $f$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]).

[F4] For scalar-valued $f$, its gradient is $\nabla f=(\partial_0f,\ldots,\partial_{m-1}f)$ ([[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]).

[F5] A scalar $f$ is of class $C^k$ on $U$ when, for every word $(i_1,\ldots,i_r)$ of coordinate indices with $0\le r\le k$, the iterated derivative $\partial_{i_r}\cdots\partial_{i_1}f$ exists and is continuous on $U$ ([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]).

[L1] If $f$ is $C^2$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^m$, then $\partial_i\partial_jf=\partial_j\partial_if$ for every pair of coordinate indices ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Every component of $F$ is $C^2$, so by [F5] every iterated derivative $\partial_i\partial_jF_a$ exists and is continuous on $U$. Hence each coordinate of $\operatorname{curl}F$, being a difference of first partial derivatives of components of $F$ by [F1], has continuous first partial derivatives, so $\operatorname{curl}F$ is $C^1$ and $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}F$ is defined; likewise $\operatorname{div}F$ is $C^1$ by [F2], so $\nabla\operatorname{div}F$ is defined by [F4]; and $\Delta F$ is defined by [F3]. [given, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5]

2.1 By [F1] applied twice, the first coordinate of $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}F$ is $\partial_y(\operatorname{curl}F)_z-\partial_z(\operatorname{curl}F)_y=\partial_y(\partial_xF_y-\partial_yF_x)-\partial_z(\partial_zF_x-\partial_xF_z)$, that is $\partial_y\partial_xF_y-\partial_y\partial_yF_x-\partial_z\partial_zF_x+\partial_z\partial_xF_z$. [step 1.1, F1, algebra]

3.1 Adding and subtracting the single term $\partial_x\partial_xF_x$ rewrites step 2.1 as $\bigl(\partial_x\partial_xF_x+\partial_y\partial_xF_y+\partial_z\partial_xF_z\bigr)-\bigl(\partial_x\partial_xF_x+\partial_y\partial_yF_x+\partial_z\partial_zF_x\bigr)$. [step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 By [L1], $\partial_y\partial_xF_y=\partial_x\partial_yF_y$ and $\partial_z\partial_xF_z=\partial_x\partial_zF_z$, so the first bracket of step 3.1 is $\partial_x\bigl(\partial_xF_x+\partial_yF_y+\partial_zF_z\bigr)=\partial_x\operatorname{div}F$, the first coordinate of $\nabla\operatorname{div}F$ by [F2] and [F4]; the second bracket is $\Delta F_x$, the first coordinate of $\Delta F$ by [F3]. Hence the first coordinate of $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}F$ is that of $\nabla\operatorname{div}F-\Delta F$. [step 3.1, L1, F2, F3, F4]

4.2 In the second coordinate, [F1] gives $\partial_z(\operatorname{curl}F)_x-\partial_x(\operatorname{curl}F)_z=\partial_z\partial_yF_z-\partial_z\partial_zF_y-\partial_x\partial_xF_y+\partial_x\partial_yF_x$; adding and subtracting $\partial_y\partial_yF_y$ and applying [L1] to $\partial_z\partial_yF_z=\partial_y\partial_zF_z$ and $\partial_x\partial_yF_x=\partial_y\partial_xF_x$ turns it into $\partial_y\operatorname{div}F-\Delta F_y$. In the third coordinate, [F1] gives $\partial_x(\operatorname{curl}F)_y-\partial_y(\operatorname{curl}F)_x=\partial_x\partial_zF_x-\partial_x\partial_xF_z-\partial_y\partial_yF_z+\partial_y\partial_zF_y$; adding and subtracting $\partial_z\partial_zF_z$ and applying [L1] to $\partial_x\partial_zF_x=\partial_z\partial_xF_x$ and $\partial_y\partial_zF_y=\partial_z\partial_yF_y$ turns it into $\partial_z\operatorname{div}F-\Delta F_z$. [step 2.1, step 3.1, L1, F1, F2, F3, F4]

5.1 All three coordinates of $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}F$ agree with those of $\nabla\operatorname{div}F-\Delta F$ at every point of $U$, which is the asserted identity. The hypothesis that $F$ is $C^2$ is used in step 1.1, so that all three expressions are defined, and in steps 4.1 and 4.2 as the hypothesis of [L1]. [step 4.1, step 4.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **The added and subtracted term is what makes the identity close.** The expansion of $(\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}F)_x$ contains no pure second derivative $\partial_x\partial_xF_x$, while both $\nabla\operatorname{div}F$ and $\Delta F$ do; that one term belongs to both groups and cancels between them, which is why it can be inserted at will and why neither side alone matches the expansion.

## Statement

For every real $x$,
$$\sin(-x)=-\sin x,\qquad\cos(-x)=\cos x,\qquad\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1.$$
Consequently $|\sin x|\le1$ and $|\cos x|\le1$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A real $x$.

[L1] For all real $u,v$, $\sin(u+v)=\sin u\cos v+\cos u\sin v$ and $\cos(u+v)=\cos u\cos v-\sin u\sin v$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]]).

[L2] The derivative identities and values at zero hold ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]).

[L3] The algebra of derivatives and the zero-derivative theorem hold ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]]).

[L4] Differentiability implies continuity ([[cor-differentiable-implies-continuous]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The derivative of $F(x)=\sin^2x+\cos^2x$ is $2\sin x\cos x-2\cos x\sin x=0$. [L2, L3, algebra]

2.1 Step 1.1 makes $F$ differentiable everywhere, hence continuous by [L4]. The zero-derivative theorem therefore makes $F$ constant, and $F(0)=1$, proving $\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1$; each square is then at most $1$. [step 1.1, L2, L3, L4, algebra]

3.1 Applying the addition formulas at $x+(-x)=0$ gives $$0=\sin x\cos(-x)+\cos x\sin(-x),\qquad 1=\cos x\cos(-x)-\sin x\sin(-x).$$ The coefficient matrix squares to the identity by step 2.1, so these equations give $\cos(-x)=\cos x$ and $\sin(-x)=-\sin x$. [L1, L2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Definition

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

## Remarks

- **This is an axiom, not a theorem.** The results on this page prove
  equivalences and consequences from AC; they do not assume an independence
  theorem in order to define or use it. [[rem-choice-ledger]] records only the
  implications and proof costs established by local results.
- Being an axiom, AC carries no well-definedness obligation, which is why this
  item has no `justified_by`.
- The case of a family listed by a natural number, which is the finite case once
  finiteness is defined, is a theorem of ZF and needs no axiom
  ([[lem-finite-choice]]). AC is exactly the extension of that theorem to
  arbitrary index sets, and the gap between the two is not a matter of degree:
  [[ex-russells-socks]] exhibits the difference concretely.
- "ZFC" abbreviates ZF together with AC. A result that invokes AC should say so
  where it is stated, so that a reader can tell which theorems are choice-free;
  that bookkeeping is the purpose of [[rem-choice-ledger]].
  [[rem-choice-strengths]] records the narrower, locally proved upper bound for
  the ultrafilter lemma. Its exact reverse implications wait for the later
  Boolean-algebra and symmetric-model development.

## Definition

Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $m,q\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^q$. A map $f:U\to\mathbb R^q$ is of class $C^k$ when each component is of class $C^k$. Each scalar component uses the word-derivative convention of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], whose source dimension is positive. The map is **smooth**, or $C^\infty$, when it is $C^k$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $U,V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open. A bijection $f:U\to V$ is a **$C^k$ diffeomorphism** when both $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are $C^k$. For $k\ge1$, a **local $C^k$ diffeomorphism at $a\in U$** is a restriction $f|_P:P\to Q$ between open neighbourhoods of $a$ and $f(a)$ that is a $C^k$ diffeomorphism. At $k=1$ this agrees with [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]: continuous first partial derivatives give the required total derivative by [[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], while continuity of the total derivative gives continuity of its matrix entries and hence of the first partial derivatives.

## Definition

Every $z\in\mathbb C$ has unique coordinates $z=a+bi$
([[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]]). Define
$$\operatorname{Re}z=a,\qquad \operatorname{Im}z=b,\qquad \overline z=a-bi,$$
and define its **modulus** by
$$|z|=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}.$$
The real numbers are least-upper-bound complete
([[cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete]]), so the nonnegative square root exists and
is unique by [[thm-of-square-roots]].

## Definition

Let $\iota_{\mathbb R}\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ be the canonical-natural map
of [[def-canonical-natural]], and let $j\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be the real
embedding $j(x)=x+i0$ from [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. For every
$n\in\mathbb N$, the factorial $n!$ is nonzero by
[[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], so
$\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!)>0$ by [[lem-of-naturals-positive]] and consequently
$j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))\ne0$ in the complex field
[[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]].

For $z\in\mathbb C$, define
$$ \exp z:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))}. $$
whenever this complex series converges. Inside a complex expression we
abbreviate the embedded denominator $j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))$ by $n!$, so the
same definition may be written $\exp z=\sum z^n/n!$ without identifying a
natural number with a complex number. Powers and series are those of
[[def-complex-integer-powers]] and
[[def-complex-series-power-series-and-absolute-convergence]]. The convergence
for every $z\in\mathbb C$ is discharged by
[[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]].

## Definition

Let $(X,\mathcal A)$ be a measurable space. A **complex measure** on
$(X,\mathcal A)$ is a function
$$\nu:\mathcal A\longrightarrow\mathbb C$$
such that:

1. $\nu(\varnothing)=0$;
2. for every pairwise disjoint sequence $(E_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ in
   $\mathcal A$,
   $$\nu\left(\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}E_n\right)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty \nu(E_n)$$
   in $\mathbb C$.

The codomain is the field $\mathbb C$
([[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]]), so a complex measure is finite-valued by
definition: there is no complex number called $+\infty$ or $-\infty$ to allow.

## Definition

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

## Remarks

- **The two formulations are equivalent, and the passage between them uses no
  choice.** Given an at most countable family $\mathcal{F}$ of nonempty sets,
  either $\mathcal{F} = \varnothing$, where the empty function is a choice
  function, or a surjection $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathcal{F}$ exists
  ([[lem-countable-iff-surjection-from-n]]); applying the indexed form to
  $X_n := s(n)$ gives $f$ with $f(n) \in s(n)$, and
  $g(S) := f(\min\{\, n : s(n) = S \,\})$ is a choice function for $\mathcal{F}$,
  the minimum being canonical by [[thm-well-ordering-principle]]. Conversely a
  choice function $g$ on the at most countable family $\{\, X_n : n \in \mathbb{N} \,\}$
  gives $f(n) := g(X_n)$.

- **AC implies countable choice.** The Axiom of Choice
  ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) applies to the family of values of any sequence of
  nonempty sets; composing the resulting choice function with the sequence
  gives the function required above.

- **Dependent choices and independent choices have different input data.**
  Countable choice selects from a family fixed in advance. Dependent choice
  instead asks for a sequence following an entire relation, where the available
  successors depend on the preceding term. The later
  [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] proves
  $\mathrm{AC}\Rightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Rightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ in ZF.
  This remark makes no assertion about reversing either implication.

- **A locally proved failure comparison appears later.**
  [[cor-relative-consistency-of-feferman-levy-choice-failures-over-zf]] proves
  the external implication from consistency of ZF to consistency of
  $\mathrm{ZF}+\neg\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, together with the stated
  Feferman–Levy properties. Hence, if ZF is consistent, it cannot prove
  countable choice: a ZF proof would also hold in that consistent extension.
  This is a conditional consistency comparison, not an assertion that
  countable choice fails in the present development.

- **Being an axiom, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ carries no well-definedness obligation**,
  which is why this item has no `justified_by`. Its role in this library is
  bookkeeping: [[thm-countable-union-of-countable]] assumes it and flags the
  exact step that spends it. No necessity claim is inferred from that proof.

- Every result *proved* on this page other than
  [[thm-countable-union-of-countable]] is a theorem of ZF alone. In particular
  [[lem-subset-of-countable]], [[lem-countable-iff-surjection-from-n]],
  [[thm-schroder-bernstein]], [[thm-rationals-countable]], [[thm-cantor-powerset]]
  and [[thm-r-uncountable]] are choice free, and each says so.

## Definition

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $F=(F_0,\ldots,F_{n-1}):U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^1$ in the componentwise Euclidean sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. Then the **divergence** of $F$ is $\operatorname{div}F:=\sum_{i<n}\partial_iF_i$, the function $U\to\mathbb R$ whose value at $p$ is $\sum_{i<n}\partial_iF_i(p)$. The partial derivatives are those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and the sum is the finite sum used throughout [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Since each $\partial_iF_i$ is continuous on $U$, so is $\operatorname{div}F$.

Now let $n=3$ and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^1$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$. Following [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], write the three coordinates of a point and of a vector as $x,y,z$ rather than $0,1,2$, so that $F=(F_x,F_y,F_z)$ means $F=(F_0,F_1,F_2)$ and $\partial_x,\partial_y,\partial_z$ are $\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2$. With that naming, the **curl** of $F$ is $\operatorname{curl}F:=(\partial_yF_z-\partial_zF_y,\ \partial_zF_x-\partial_xF_z,\ \partial_xF_y-\partial_yF_x)$, a map $U\to\mathbb R^3$ each of whose coordinates is continuous on $U$. In this naming the divergence reads $\operatorname{div}F=\partial_xF_x+\partial_yF_y+\partial_zF_z$.

Both operators are defined pointwise from the first partial derivatives of the components, so no differentiability of $F$ beyond $C^1$ is used and no orientation or metric structure enters beyond the standard coordinates of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]. For a $C^1$ scalar function $f$ on $U$, the gradient $\nabla f=(\partial_0f,\ldots,\partial_{n-1}f)$ is that of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]; in the three-coordinate naming, $\nabla f=(\partial_xf,\partial_yf,\partial_zf)$.

## Remarks

- **Why the curl is only defined in three coordinates.** If $A=JF-(JF)^{\mathsf T}$ with the row-component Jacobian convention, then the curl coordinates are $A_{zy}$, $A_{xz}$ and $A_{yx}$. Thus the curl is encoded, with fixed signs, by the three independent off-diagonal entries of $A$ (or by twice those entries if “antisymmetric part” means $A/2$). In $n$ coordinates there are $n(n-1)/2$ independent entries. Only at $n=3$ is that number again $n$, which is what allows the collection to be read as a vector in the same space. The divergence has no such restriction and is defined for every $n\ge1$.

- **The word "divergence" here is about vector fields.** It has nothing to do with the divergence of a sequence or of a series; the two senses share only the word.

- **Placement of the minus sign in the second coordinate.** Some presentations write the middle coordinate as $-(\partial_xF_z-\partial_zF_x)$. That is the same real number as $\partial_zF_x-\partial_xF_z$, and the form displayed above is the one whose three coordinates read off the coordinate formula of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]] in the same cyclic pattern.

snapshot.title: Complex plane-wave fields: real parts of complex exponentials
snapshot.statement: Fix $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, $\omega>0$ and $\mathbf e,\mathbf b\in\mathbb C^3$. Writing $\exp$ for the complex exponential, $\operatorname{Re}$ for the real part and $\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x$ for the Euclidean inner product, define for each $t\in\mathbb R$ the real vector fields $$\mathbf x\mapsto\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\mathbf e\exp(i(\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x-\omega t))\bigr],\qquad \mathbf x\mapsto\operatorname{Re}\bigl[\mathbf b\exp(i(\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x-\omega t))\bigr]$$ on $\mathbb R^3$, componentwise. Complex notation is an encoding of real fields and of real linear equations; the complex object is not itself a physical field, and real parts, imaginary parts and complex conjugation are explicit operations.

No electromagnetic interpretation is asserted; that is a later model choice.

snapshot.title: The electric and magnetic fields as fixed-time spatial vector fields
snapshot.statement: Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its spatial Euclidean structure and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $k\ge1$. An electric field of class $C^k$ on the region is a map $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is of class $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; a magnetic field of class $C^k$ is a map $B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of the same class. At fixed $t\in I$ the maps $E(\cdot,t),B(\cdot,t):\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ are real spatial vector fields on the region $\Omega$, read in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame. The framework uses: $C^1$ fields in the classical Maxwell branch, $C^2$ fields where second or mixed time-space derivatives of the fields appear, and $C^\infty$ fields in the smooth existence branches; every statement carries its own regularity and no regularity beyond it is asserted. Conventions: (a) $E$ is a polar vector and $B$ an axial vector relative to the orientation of the spatial basis; the changes of inertial description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] are proper and orientation preserving, so orientation-reversing descriptions are not among them; (b) the fields are defined by their values on $\Omega\times I$, and no value at a point of singular source support is asserted; (c) $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$ and $B$ carries T; (d) the identification of the pair $(E,B)$ with the components of an alternating two-form, including its transformation behaviour, is made in [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and is not presupposed here.
snapshot.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition: the fields are maps on the product $\Omega\times I$ of the laboratory region with a stated class of regularity, and their fixed-time readings are spatial vector fields in the frame basis. The regularity notion is that of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; the polar/axial convention and the exclusion of pointwise values at singular source support are conventions recorded explicitly rather than used implicitly. No differential equation and no derived quantity is introduced by this definition.
