after_snapshot.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] and [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] ([[def-countable-choice]]), whose trace qualification is used in clause (d); the full-Choice modal branch of the latter is not used. Adopt the scalar aperture model and its notation from [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]]: frequency $\omega>0$, $k=\omega/c$, aperture radius $a>0$, finite complex aperture distribution $\alpha$ supported in the planar aperture $S\subset\{y_3=0\}\cap\{y:|y|\le a\}$, model field $u=G_k*\alpha$, real field $U(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ and $T=2\pi/\omega$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-complex-exponential]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]], [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]). Set $I(x):=(1/2)|u(x)|^2$. Then: (a) [Model field and Fraunhofer estimate] $u$ is $C^\infty$ on the half-space $\{x_3>0\}$ and on $\mathbb R^3\setminus S$, satisfies $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ there, and is outgoing in the sense of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]]: for $x=rn$ with $r\ge2a$ and $n\in S^2$, $$u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)+O\Bigl(\frac{\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}}{r}\Bigl[\frac ar+\frac{ka^2}{r}\Bigr]\Bigr)$$ uniformly in direction, and $r(\partial_ru-iku)=O(r^{-1})$ uniformly. (b) [Fresnel estimate] write $y_t=(y_1,y_2)$ and $\xi=(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ for transverse vectors; for the planar aperture and observation $x=(\xi_1,\xi_2,z)$ with $z>0$, $b\ge0$, $|\xi|\le b$ and any declared fixed small-angle range $(a+b)/z\le\eta_0<1$, where $0<\eta_0<1$, the Fresnel approximation replaces $R=|x-y|$ by $z+|\xi-y_t|^2/(2z)$ and $1/R$ by $1/z$ in the model integral with phase error $O(k(a+b)^4/z^3)$, relative amplitude error $O((a+b)^2/z^2)$ and absolute field error $O(\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}z^{-1}[(a+b)^2/z^2+k(a+b)^4/z^3])$. (c) [Intensity and error transfer] at every $x$ with $x_3>0$ the model period average satisfies $\frac1T\int_0^TU(x,s)^2\,ds=I(x)$ ([[lem-em-period-average]]). If $u_{\rm approx}$ is any approximation of $u$ with $|u_{\rm approx}(x)-u(x)|\le\delta(x)$, then $|\frac12|u_{\rm approx}(x)|^2-I(x)|\le\frac12\delta(x)(|u(x)|+|u_{\rm approx}(x)|)$; if moreover $u(x)\ne0$ and $|u_{\rm approx}(x)-u(x)|\le\epsilon(x)|u(x)|$, the relative intensity error is at most $2\epsilon(x)+\epsilon(x)^2$. In particular the Fraunhofer and Fresnel field errors of (a) and (b) bound the corresponding intensity errors; no new approximation is introduced by passing to $I$. (d) [Trace and scope] the aperture distribution $\alpha$ is an adopted model datum and is not identified with the exact Maxwell boundary data on the screen; assigning both $u$ and $\partial_nu$ on the aperture independently does not produce a well-posed exact boundary problem ([[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]]). The construction ignores polarization and aperture back-reaction, makes no claim that $u$ or $U$ satisfies the Maxwell equations exactly, and makes no measured-intensity, apparatus, sampling or empirical claim; only comparisons of $I$ between observation points are read as model predictions.
after_snapshot.strategy: The theorem instantiates the mathematical field estimates of [[lem-em-outgoing-source-helmholtz-and-diffraction]] at the adopted model datum of [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]]. (a) The model field is the supplier's convolution. Choose any open containing ball of radius $A>a$ to obtain its off-support smoothness and Helmholtz equation. For the advertised sharp-radius endpoint, argue directly for every $|y|\le a$ and $r\ge2a$. Write $R=|rn-y|$, so $R\ge r-a\ge r/2$. For $h(s)=|rn-sy|$, the exact norm derivative formula from the supplier gives $|h''(s)|\le2a^2/(r-a)\le4a^2/r$; twice FTC therefore gives $|R-r+n\cdot y|\le2a^2/r$, and $|r/R-1|\le2a/r$. The supplier's real phase bound $|e^{i\theta}-1|\le|\theta|$ now gives $$\left|G_k(rn-y)-\frac{e^{ikr}e^{-ikn\cdot y}}{4\pi r}\right|\le\frac1{2\pi r}\left(\frac ar+\frac{ka^2}r\right).$$ For a bounded continuous kernel $f$ on the compact support, $|\int f\,d\alpha|\le\sup|f|\,\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}$ follows by [[prop-simple-integrals-are-bounded-by-total-variation]] and uniform finite-simple approximation in [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]; hence this pointwise bound proves the original field error, including $r=2a$. The exact derivative $\partial_rR=(r-n\cdot y)/R$ has modulus at most1 and $|\partial_rR-1|\le2a^2/r^2$. Differentiating the explicit kernel gives $r|\partial_rG_k-ikG_k|\le(\pi r)^{-1}(1+ka^2/r)$; the same finite-measure bound gives the uniform outgoing residual. All derivative passages under the source integral use the supplier's compact-product uniform difference-quotient argument, not an unsupported complex-measure dominated-convergence claim. (b) On the explicitly declared range put $d_0=a+b$ and $s=|\xi-y_t|^2/z^2\le\eta_0^2<1$. The actual supplier proof gives $|\sqrt{1+s}-1-s/2|\le s^2/8$ and $|(1+s)^{-1/2}-1|\le s/2$ by twice FTC. Consequently the phase error is at most $kd_0^4/(8z^3)$ and the relative amplitude error at most $d_0^2/(2z^2)$. The complex-measure kernel bound above gives $$|u-u_{\rm Fresnel}|\le\frac{\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}}{4\pi z}\left[\frac{d_0^2}{2z^2}+\frac{kd_0^4}{8z^3}\right],$$ which preserves and quantifies all original Fresnel estimates for the closed-support datum. (c) applies [[lem-em-period-average]] with $a=d=u(x)$: $\operatorname{Re}(u(x)e^{-i\omega t})^2$ averages to $\frac12\operatorname{Re}(u(x)\overline{u(x)})=\frac12|u(x)|^2$. The first error bound is the identity $\frac12\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|^2-|u|^2\bigr|=\frac12\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|-|u|\bigr|(|u_{\rm approx}|+|u|)$ together with $\bigl||u_{\rm approx}|-|u|\bigr|\le|u_{\rm approx}-u|$, obtained by applying the triangle inequality of [[lem-complex-conjugation-and-modulus-laws]] in both directions; the relative bound is $||u_{\rm approx}|^2-|u|^2|/|u|^2\le\epsilon(2+\epsilon)$. No choice principle beyond that carried by the suppliers is used. (d) reproduces the trace distinction of [[lem-em-helmholtz-boundary-representation]] and the model-scope declarations of the postulate; the intensity reading is the declared one, so no radiometric claim is added. The Countable Choice hypothesis is inherited from the cited suppliers; the intensity computation of (c) uses only the choice-free period-average lemma.

after_snapshot.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as carried by [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]], whose variational, Sobolev-compactness and compact-spectral steps use it; the algebraic computations below use no further choice. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded open set with $C^\infty$ boundary, $D:=\mathbb R^3\setminus\overline O$ connected, $k>0$, $\omega:=ck$ with $c$ the vacuum speed of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and $R>0$ with $\overline O\subset B_R(0)$; let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open with $\overline D\subseteq V$, and let $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc},\widetilde B_{\rm inc})$ be a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on $V$ ([[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]). Plane-wave instances are provided by [[pthm-em-plane-wave-maxwell]]: if $\kappa\cdot e=0$, $b=\kappa\times e/\omega$ and $|\kappa|=\omega/c$, then $(\widetilde E_{\rm inc},\widetilde B_{\rm inc})(x)=(e\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x},b\,e^{i\kappa\cdot x})$ satisfies the four phasor equations on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-em-plane-wave-definition]]). Adopt the ideal perfectly conducting (PEC) boundary model: the tangential component of the total electric field vanishes on $\partial O$. This is a declared idealization of the stationary interface conditions of [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] with vanishing fields inside the conductor; it is not one of the finite-conductivity branches of [[post-em-material-closure]], and the induced surface charge and current are neither prescribed nor determined here. Let $e_T$ be the tangential projection of $-\widetilde E_{\rm inc}$ on $\partial O$, and let $\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ be the unique $C^\infty$ field on $\overline D$ of [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] with $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ and $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ on $D$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$ and that lemma's outgoing modal condition on $S_R$. Set $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}:=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ and, on $D$, $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}:=\widetilde E_{\rm inc}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$, $\widetilde B_{\rm tot}:=\widetilde B_{\rm inc}+\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$. Then: (a) [Phasor Maxwell] $(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ and $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ are $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pairs on $D$; and for every $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair $(\widetilde E,\widetilde B)$ on an open set $O'\subseteq\mathbb R^3$, the associated real fields of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]] satisfy on $O'\times\mathbb R$ the smooth-branch vacuum Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho\equiv0$ and $J\equiv0$. Consequently the associated real total fields $E_{\rm tot},B_{\rm tot}$ satisfy those source-free equations on $D\times\mathbb R$. (b) [PEC boundary condition] the tangential trace of $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}$ on $\partial O$ vanishes; hence for every unit normal field $n$ of $\partial O$ the associated real total electric field $E_{\rm tot}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E_{\rm tot}(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ ([[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]) satisfies $n\times E_{\rm tot}=0$ on $\partial O\times\mathbb R$. (c) [Uniqueness] if $(\widetilde E',\widetilde B')$ is a $C^\infty$ frequency-$\omega$ source-free vacuum phasor pair on an open set $V'\supseteq\overline D$ that is outgoing on $S_R$ in the modal sense of the vector Helmholtz lemma and has tangential trace $e_T$ on $\partial O$, then $(\widetilde E',\widetilde B')=(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ on $D$; equivalently $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$ is the unique total source-free phasor pair in the corresponding $C^\infty$ closure class with that prescribed incident phasor, vanishing tangential electric trace, and outgoing scattered correction $\widetilde E_{\rm tot}-\widetilde E_{\rm inc}$ in the lemma's modal class. The total field itself is not required to be outgoing; an incident plane wave is generally not outgoing. (d) [Scope] one positive frequency $\omega=ck$, one smooth bounded stationary PEC obstacle with connected exterior, and $C^\infty$ incident and scattered classes only; no lossy, impedance, nonsmooth or dispersive obstacle, no determination of the induced surface charge or current, no radiation-zone amplitude or far-field asymptotics beyond the lemma's outgoing modal class, no point or singular source, no finite-energy or empirical claim.
after_snapshot.strategy: Assume the Axiom of Choice exactly through [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] (its symmetry/coercivity, compactness and compact-spectral steps); all other steps are pointwise algebra. (a) For the scattered pair: $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$ is the boundary-problem condition; $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=i\omega\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ holds by the definition of $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$; $\operatorname{div}\widetilde B_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B_{\rm scat}=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}(\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=(i\omega)^{-1}(\nabla\operatorname{div}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}-\Delta\widetilde E_{\rm scat})=(i\omega)^{-1}k^2\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ by [[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]], [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=0$; the sum of two solutions of the linear system is a solution by [[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]. The real-field Maxwell statement is clause (c) of [[lem-em-phasor-real-part-calculus-and-equivalence]] with the constant $c$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]], combined with the identification of its real system with the zero-source smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; the incident pair is a pair on $V$, hence on $D$. (b) The tangential traces satisfy $\widetilde E_{\rm tot,tang}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+\widetilde E_{\rm scat,tang}=\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+e_T=0$ on $\partial O$; the associated real field is the real part of the tangential trace, hence vanishes (the encoding and real-part calculus are those of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]] and [[lem-em-phasor-real-part-calculus-and-equivalence]]). (c) For a candidate phasor pair, $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E'=i\omega\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B'=\omega^2c^{-2}\widetilde E'=k^2\widetilde E'$, and $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E'=0$. The componentwise real/imaginary curl-curl identity thus gives $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E'=0$. Its prescribed tangential trace and outgoing correction are the declared boundary class. Hence the candidate $\widetilde E'$ satisfies all hypotheses of the uniqueness assertion of [[lem-em-exterior-vector-helmholtz-mixed-boundary-existence]] for the same tangential data, so $\widetilde E'=\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$; then $\widetilde B'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ by the third phasor equation of [[def-em-monochromatic-source-free-phasors]]. For the total-field formulation subtract the fixed incident pair: linearity gives a source-free correction with tangential trace $e_T$, and the required outgoing condition is on that correction. Conversely adding the fixed incident pair recovers the total boundary condition. Thus uniqueness transfers exactly to total-minus-incident outgoing; it does not impose the outgoing class on an incident plane wave or on their total. (d) records the exact scope; in particular the ideal PEC condition is adopted, not derived, and the material-closure branches of [[post-em-material-closure]] contain no $\sigma\to\infty$ branch, while [[pthm-em-material-stationary-jumps]] supplies only the stationary-interface idealization context.

after_snapshot.title: Uniform rectangular aperture: the Fraunhofer sinc-squared pattern
after_snapshot.statement: Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]] and by the Riemann-Lebesgue comparison and Fubini suppliers used in the integral reduction below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the scalar aperture model of [[post-em-scalar-aperture-model]] and [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]], with frequency $\omega>0$, $k=\omega/c$, aperture plane $y_3=0$, model field $u=G_k*\alpha$ and $I(x)=\frac12|u(x)|^2$. Fix $a>0$, $b>0$ and $A_0\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$; identify the rectangle $R:=[-a,a]\times[-b,b]\subset\mathbb R^2$ with the planar aperture $\{(y_1,y_2,0):(y_1,y_2)\in R\}$ and take the **uniform rectangular aperture distribution** let $\iota:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^3$ be $\iota(y_1,y_2)=(y_1,y_2,0)$, and define its plane-embedding pushforward $$\alpha(E):=A_0\,\lambda_2(R\cap\iota^{-1}(E))\qquad(E\subseteq\mathbb R^3\text{ Borel}).$$ This is a finite complex measure on $\mathbb R^3$, supported on the embedded compact rectangle $S=\iota(R)$ with $|y|\le a':=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$ and total variation $\|\alpha\|_{\rm TV}=4ab|A_0|$ ([[def-multidimensional-rectangle-and-volume]], [[def-measure-with-density]], [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]). Then: (a) [Fraunhofer amplitude] with $\operatorname{sinc}\xi:=\sin\xi/\xi$ for $\xi\ne0$ and $\operatorname{sinc}0:=1$, the Fraunhofer amplitude factor of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a) is exactly $$\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)=4abA_0\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)\qquad(n=(n_1,n_2,n_3)\in S^2),$$ an identity for every direction $n$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-complex-exponential]], [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]], [[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]], [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]). (b) [Fraunhofer intensity] in the Fraunhofer regime of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a) with aperture radius $a':=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, i.e. for $r\ge2a'$, the model intensity is $$I_{\rm F}(rn)=\frac{a^2b^2|A_0|^2}{2\pi^2r^2}\operatorname{sinc}^2(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}^2(kb\,n_2)$$ up to the Fraunhofer absolute error of that theorem, transferred to $I$ by its clause (c). The pattern vanishes exactly where $ka\,n_1\in\pi\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ or $kb\,n_2\in\pi\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, and, as a mathematical pattern on all $S^2$, has its global maximum exactly at the two poles $n=(0,0,\pm1)$. The model observes only $x_3>0$; its allowed directions have $n_3>0$, where the central maximum is only $n=(0,0,1)$. (c) [Scope] this is an exact computation inside the adopted ideal scalar model, not a measured diffraction record: no absolute radiometric calibration, polarization content, screen interaction, apparatus model or sampling law is asserted, and the Fraunhofer/Fresnel error bounds of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]] are inherited rather than re-estimated.
after_snapshot.strategy: (a) The continuous embedding $\iota$ has Borel inverse images by [[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]. Disjoint Borel sets have disjoint inverse images; countable additivity of $\lambda_2$ therefore proves directly that the displayed $\alpha$ is a complex measure as in [[def-complex-measure]]. It is supported on $S=\iota(R)$. For every countable partition, the sum of the moduli of its values is $|A_0|\lambda_2(R)=4ab|A_0|$ by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], so [[def-total-variation-of-a-signed-or-complex-measure]] gives the stated finite total variation. For a simple Borel $f$ on $\mathbb R^3$ the defining sum gives $\int f\,d\alpha=A_0\int_Rf(\iota(y))\,d\lambda_2(y)$; uniform finite-simple approximations of any bounded Borel $f$ and the total-variation bound pass this identity to the integrals of [[def-integration-against-a-signed-or-complex-measure]]. Thus the plane measure is correctly typed for the three-dimensional model. For $f(y)=e^{-ik(n_1y_1+n_2y_2)}$ (the $y_3$-coordinate is zero on the aperture, and $n\cdot y=n_1y_1+n_2y_2$ by [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), $f$ is continuous on the compact rectangle $R$ ([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]), so [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] identifies the Lebesgue integral with the Riemann double integral; [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]] factors it into the product of the two one-dimensional integrals. For $n_1\ne0$, the one-dimensional integral is $\int_{-a}^a e^{-ikn_1y_1}\,dy_1=2\sin(ka\,n_1)/(kn_1)=2a\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)$ by [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] for the affine phase $y_1\mapsto-kn_1y_1$, applied to the real and imaginary parts via [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]; for $n_1=0$ it equals $2a=2a\operatorname{sinc}0$ by the separately defined value, so the formula holds for every direction. The second factor is analogous, giving the displayed product $4abA_0\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)$. (b) Insert the product amplitude into the Fraunhofer expression $u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}d\alpha(y)+$error of [[pthm-em-scalar-aperture-diffraction]](a), square the modulus and use $I=\frac12|u|^2$; the modulus of the amplitude is $4ab|A_0||\operatorname{sinc}(ka\,n_1)||\operatorname{sinc}(kb\,n_2)|$, so $|u_{\rm F}|^2=\frac{a^2b^2|A_0|^2}{\pi^2r^2}\operatorname{sinc}^2(ka\,n_1)\operatorname{sinc}^2(kb\,n_2)$ and the factor $\frac12$ gives the displayed $I_{\rm F}$. The zero assertion follows from [[thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period]] and the separate value at0. To prove the exact maxima, $|\sin x|<|x|$ for every $x\ne0$: for $x>0$ set $\delta=\min\{x/3,\pi/6\}>0$. On $[\delta,2\delta]$, the cosine signs and strict monotonicity of [[thm-sine-cosine-signs-monotonicity-and-ranges]] give $|\cos t|\le\cos\delta<1$, while globally $|\cos t|\le1$. FTC and the Riemann integral triangle/monotonicity estimate (applied to $-|\cos|\le\cos\le|\cos|$) give $|\sin x|\le\int_0^x|\cos t|\,dt\le x-\delta(1-\cos\delta)<x$; continuous integrability and subinterval additivity are supplied by [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]] and [[thm-additivity-over-subintervals]]. Negative $x$ follows from sine oddness in [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]. Thus $|\operatorname{sinc}x|=1$ exactly at0, and since $k,a,b>0$ the product attains its maximum exactly when $n_1=n_2=0$, the two spherical poles. Only the positive pole belongs to the model upper half-space. The embedded corners have norm exactly $a'=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$; the support lies in the closed radius set $|y|\le a'$, so the parent theorem's directly proved closed-support estimate applies at the unchanged endpoint $r\ge2a'$; clause (c) of the theorem transfers the field error to $I$. (c) is the scope of the model; no additional approximation is introduced. The computation uses only the standard Riemann/Lebesgue and trigonometric suppliers listed in the dependencies; the Countable Choice assumption is exactly the one carried by the Riemann-Lebesgue comparison and Fubini interfaces, with no additional choice.
